d.d: Supposing that, assuming that, in the circumstances that; suppositive used to introduce a condition that may be (or prove to be) either true or false.
d.x: I'll do it next week if I have time.

d.d: A keyword that invokes conditional processing: in the event that a given condition is true, execute the given statement(s) (otherwise execute other statements).
d.x: if A then B else C

d.d: Supposing that; used with past or past perfect subjunctive to indicate a counterfactual or hypothetical condition.
d.x: If she hadn't told me, I wouldn't know.

d.d: An uncertainty, possibility, condition, doubt etc.
d.x: The board can't approve this project; there are too many ifs.
